speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to evaluate the skin condition on your left dorsal hand. To begin, can you describe when you first noticed the rash and what it looks like?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing your history. Given your age, diabetes, and outdoor activities, have you noticed any specific triggers like sun exposure, insect bites, or new soaps that might be related to the rash on your left dorsal hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with a history of sun exposure is clinically characteristic. Given your lack of pain and your outdoor lifestyle, I recommend a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out squamous cell carcinoma.
